Consult Summary:
- 50-year-old woman with 5–6 days of dry, persistent cough and rhinorrhea with chills and myalgias; initial diarrhea resolved. No dyspnea or chest pain. Clinician impression: likely viral illness; supportive care advised with short-term work absence and return precautions.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Persistent dry cough and runny nose.
- Timeline:
  - Onset: ~5–6 days ago.
  - Course: Cough continuous, present day and night; keeps patient awake. Rhinorrhea ongoing. Early diarrhea at onset resolved after a short duration; cough persists.
- Character/associated symptoms:
  - Cough: Dry; no sputum. Nighttime disturbance.
  - Upper respiratory: Runny nose; sore throat only from coughing irritation; no odynophagia.
  - Ears: No pain, blockage, or discharge.
  - Chest/respiratory: No day-to-day breathlessness; no chest pain. Breathing only feels labored during coughing fits.
  - Constitutional: Chills/shivering, fatigue, lethargy, generalized myalgias (arms and legs). No documented fever (no temperature measured).
  - GI: No nausea or vomiting. Initial diarrhea at symptom onset; resolved. Appetite okay.
  - GU: No urinary symptoms; drinking fluids normally now.
- Pertinent negatives: No chest pain, no dyspnea with routine activity, no ear pain/discharge, no nausea/vomiting, diarrhea resolved.

Past Medical History:
- Type 2 diabetes mellitus: Patient reports condition is under control with regular checkups.
- Hypertension: Patient reports condition is under control with regular checkups.

Medications:
- Metformin — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Lisinopril — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.

Social History:
- Living situation: Lives with partner; partner well without similar illness.
- Occupation: IT developer; largely sedentary job. Took 1 day off initially; has been working despite symptoms.
- Tobacco: Former smoker; quit ~6 months ago.
- Alcohol: Wine ~2–3 glasses on up to 3 evenings per week; clinician advised reduction.
- Stress: Not more than usual.

Family History:
- Father with type 2 diabetes.

Physical Examination:
- Not documented.

Investigations:
- None discussed.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute viral upper respiratory illness with dry cough and rhinorrhea; associated chills, fatigue, myalgias; initial diarrhea resolved; no red flags (no chest pain, no significant dyspnea).
  - Plan:
    - Supportive care: Rest, maintain hydration, take acetaminophen (paracetamol) as needed.
    - Work: Take 1–2 days off for rest; consider returning early next week if improved.
    - Expected course: Symptoms typically last ~7–10 days.
    - Follow-up: Return if not improving in 2–3 days for reassessment.
    - Red flags: Return sooner if breathing worsens or if persistent fever and cough; antibiotics may be considered if ongoing fever and cough without improvement.
- Issue 2: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, chronic, patient reports controlled with regular follow-up.
  - Plan: Continue current management; no changes discussed during this visit.
- Issue 3: Hypertension, chronic, patient reports controlled with regular follow-up.
  - Plan: Continue current management; no changes discussed during this visit.
- Issue 4: Alcohol use counseling in context of HTN/DM.
  - Plan: Reduce intake—initially to 2 glasses per week for a few weeks, then 1 per week thereafter; aim to discontinue if able.

General Plan items:
- None beyond above.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Vitals (including temperature), physical exam, medication doses/route/frequency, vaccination status, sick-day guidance for diabetes not addressed, COVID/flu testing not discussed.
- Internal conflicts: None noted.
- Transcript quality: Some pauses and brief inaudible/elliptical sections; overall clinical content adequate.
